summary: Max Q is a 3D rocket and mission simulator that runs in any web browser. Press "Create world", choose a Mission (photograph Earth or deep space) or Sandbox (fly freely), then pick your destination on a model of the Solar System and beyond that uses the real names scientists use: Mercury, Venus, Earth, the Moon, Mars, Jupiter, the heliopause and Alpha Centauri. Next you choose a rocket - ARGO, PYRAMIS, Saturn V, Space Shuttle, or the giant COLOSSUS booster carrying a nuclear-pulse "Hydrobomb" or an antimatter deep-space ship - and fly it yourself or on autopilot. Real physics decides what happens: staging, drag, heating, g-forces and orbits. Mission goals ask you to photograph real places, and the camera checks what was really in the frame. If the rocket breaks, a "Why it failed" page explains the cause. A Settings tab switches every explanation between Beginner (age 10), Average (age 20) and Master (rocket engineer). Friends can join the same world with a share code.
details:
What it does

  • Create world: choose Mission or Sandbox. Missions: photograph Earth from orbit, or photograph deep space.
  • Universe map: pick a destination on a log-scale model with real names (Sun, Mercury, Venus, Earth, Moon, Mars, Jupiter, the heliopause, Alpha Centauri - the last only in Sandbox).
  • Six rockets: ARGO, PYRAMIS, Saturn V (S-IC, S-II, S-IVB), Space Shuttle (two solid boosters, external tank, orbiter), and COLOSSUS (8 boosters plus a core) carrying a deep-space ship.
  • Deep-space ships: a Hydrobomb (nuclear-pulse) ship whose 1,280 pulse units drift out of the bomb door and detonate behind a pusher plate, and an antimatter ship. Both are non-cylindrical, and the Hydrobomb has 10 thick shield layers mounted at the front. The pulse drive is safed below 100 km.
  • Fly it: steer the rocket yourself or use autopilot. Staging, thrust, drag, wind, heating, g-load and orbit are simulated.
  • Photo goals: press the camera button; the game checks which bodies were really in the frame, their size and the place on Earth below (real latitude and longitude).
  • Why it failed: a crash, overheating, structural break, too many g's, a missed orbit or a failed docking opens a page that explains the cause and how to fix it.
  • Settings: Beginner / Average / Master language levels for every explanation.
  • Join by code: a world code (also in the page link) lets another player load the same mission, destination and rocket.
  • Debug button: a JS console at the top-left (Ctrl+Alt+D) that works on PC, Mac and Chromebook.

How it addresses the challenge

Players make the mission decisions themselves - objective, destination, launch vehicle, propulsion - and see how each choice shapes the result: a small rocket cannot reach Jupiter; turning too hard in thick air breaks the rocket; a missed burn means a missed orbit. Failure is safe and explained, so players learn by trying again.

How it was built

HTML, JavaScript and three.js (r128) in one web page, hosted on GitHub Pages. Rocket figures are rounded public values; the Saturn V and Space Shuttle follow NASA fact sheets; the Hydrobomb follows the 1960s Project Orion nuclear-pulse study; the antimatter ship uses order-of-magnitude concept values and is labelled speculative.

Who made it

Max Q is the idea of our 10-year-old team member: the rockets, the deep-space ships, the Create world flow, the universe map, the three language levels and the "Why it failed" page all come from his design. An adult helped with accounts and the submission.

Use of AI

The code was written with AI assistance (Anthropic Claude: Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Fable 5.2), directed and tested by our team. The voice-over in the demo video was generated with an AI voice tool (Grok). No AI-generated images or video are used; the video is a screen recording of the game.

Prior work (disclosure)

Max Q started before the hackathon as an unpublished personal project of our young team member (the 3D flight engine with ARGO and PYRAMIS). During the hackathon (14-15 November 2026) we added: the Create world flow, Mission and Sandbox modes, the universe map with real names, the photo goals and camera check, Saturn V, Space Shuttle, COLOSSUS, the Hydrobomb and antimatter ships with front shields and visible pulse units, the Beginner / Average / Master settings, join-by-code, the "Why it failed" page, the debug button, and a fix for stuck keys after system shortcuts. We list this openly so the judges can decide how to weigh it.
